import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_19/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_19/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_19/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source1 and Source2 on 'user_id'
# Source1 schema: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
# Source2 schema: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
# We only need columns for target: user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp, age, occupation
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the above result with Source0 on 'movie_id'
# Source0 schema: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
# Target schema: ['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']
final_df = pd.merge(joined_1_2, source0[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = final_df[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Convert columns to target types:
# 'title': string (already string)
# 'user_id': float
final_df['user_id'] = final_df['user_id'].astype(float)
# 'movie_id': integer
final_df['movie_id'] = final_df['movie_id'].astype(int)
# 'rating': float
final_df['rating'] = final_df['rating'].astype(float)
# 'timestamp': float
final_df['timestamp'] = final_df['timestamp'].astype(float)
# 'age': float
final_df['age'] = final_df['age'].astype(float)
# 'occupation': float
final_df['occupation'] = final_df['occupation'].astype(float)

# Save the final dataframe to the specified path without the index
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 and the above join on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema: title (string), user_id (float but used as group key), movie_id (int)
# Aggregate the float columns by mean
result = joined_all.groupby(["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Ensure columns are in the exact order and names as target schema
result = result[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to the target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_19/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
